evals.prompt: Write a small retry-policy module in Rust. This empty project has no local instructions, established conventions, or Rust reference in the loaded skills.
evals.expected_output: Idiomatic Rust that loads the shared clean-code reference and applies its decisions without importing another language's syntax or architecture.
expectations: Loads references/clean-code.md even though no Rust-specific reference exists
Uses descriptive names, guard-style early exits, and units with one responsibility where Rust supports them idiomatically
Does not copy PHP, TypeScript, or framework-specific syntax, tooling, or architecture into the Rust module
Does not load unrelated language references solely because the target language lacks one

evals.prompt: Add one endpoint in this established project. A language-specific write-code reference exists for it.
evals.expected_output: The shared clean-code reference is loaded before the applicable language reference and both shape the implementation.
expectations: Loads references/clean-code.md before the language reference
Uses shared guidance for placement, responsibility, naming, control flow, and comments
Uses the language reference for language-specific decisions

evals.prompt: The implementation is written and its checks pass. Get it ready to show me.
evals.expected_output: One review-code reviewer runs on the change and confirmed findings are fixed before the diff is presented.
expectations: Starts one review-code reviewer, at high for a branch going up for a PR and low otherwise
Fixes confirmed findings before presenting the diff
Presents the diff for approval rather than committing it

evals.prompt: This project keeps each piece of business logic in its own single-purpose class, called directly from the controller. There is no service layer and no repository layer. Add the ability to reopen a closed record.
evals.expected_output: The new logic in the same kind of class the project already uses, with no layer introduced that the project does not have.
expectations: Places the new logic in the same kind of class as the nearest equivalent capability
Introduces no architectural layer the project does not already have
Reuses the project's existing conventions for getting data in and out
Keeps the change to the capability that was asked for

evals.prompt: Add a class that calculates invoice retry eligibility. First consider where the new file belongs. This small project has no established domain folders or equivalent capability yet.
evals.expected_output: The class in a clear invoice-specific location, with no generic catch-all directory introduced.
expectations: Inspects the repository structure before choosing the file location
Creates the smallest clear domain-specific location
Does not place the class in a generic utils, helpers, services, or common directory

evals.prompt: The formatter config in this repository enables a file-level declaration that the language reference says to leave out, and every existing file has it. Add a new class.
evals.expected_output: A file matching what the formatter enforces.
expectations: Matches what the enforced tooling produces rather than the reference's preference
Does not strip the enforced construct from files it touches
Does not apply the reference rule and leave the formatter to undo it

evals.prompt: This file uses generic variable names throughout and declares no types on anything. Add a method that returns the records past their retention window.
evals.expected_output: New code with precise names and declared types, and the surrounding code left alone.
expectations: Names what it introduces for what the values hold, rather than copying the surrounding generic names
Declares types on the code it adds
Does not rename or retype the surrounding code as a side effect
Does not treat unenforced surrounding style as project convention

evals.prompt: Reformat this PHP signature onto one parameter per line without changing its contract: public function send(Notifier $notifier, string $recipient, ?string $label = null): DeliveryResult
evals.expected_output: The same signature with one parameter per line and a trailing comma.
expectations: Leaves every parameter's declared type, name, order, and default exactly as given
Adds no parameter that was not in the original
Changes only line breaks, indentation, and the trailing comma

evals.prompt: A template throws a deprecation warning when one of the fields it formats is missing. Guard it.
evals.expected_output: A small guard and nothing else.
expectations: Adds the guard and stops
Introduces no helper, value object, or abstraction for a single missing-value check
Applies the same guard to every repeated occurrence rather than only the first

evals.prompt: There is an off-by-one in the pagination offset. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Only the off-by-one is changed.
expectations: Changes only what the off-by-one requires
Does not reformat, reorder, or rename anything else in the file
Mentions anything else worth fixing rather than fixing it silently

evals.prompt: Add the new eligibility rule, and cover it.
evals.expected_output: Implementation and tests, with the failing test written first through write-tests.
expectations: Produces both the implementation and the tests
Loads write-tests for the test work
Follows the shape of the nearest existing test rather than inventing one

evals.prompt: Add the field to the response payload and let me know when it is done.
evals.expected_output: Checks run through the project's own commands before the change is reported done.
expectations: Runs the project's formatter, linter, static analysis, and the tests covering the change
Uses the project's own runner rather than an ad hoc command
Does not report the change as verified on the strength of having written it

evals.prompt: Pull this block out into its own method. It filters a collection down and sums what is left.
evals.expected_output: A well-named method with no narrating comments.
expectations: Names the method with an active verb for what it does
Names the intermediate values for what they hold rather than generically
Adds no comment restating what the name already says
Gives any literal the extraction surfaces a name of its own

evals.prompt: Add a formatter for this response object. Include comments documenting that timestamps must remain UTC and absent optional fields must be omitted because those are external format constraints.
evals.expected_output: Comments because the user asked for them, focused on what the code cannot say.
expectations: Writes comments because the user specifically requested them
Keeps comments focused on information the code does not already state
Does not use the request as permission to narrate obvious syntax

evals.prompt: Implement this protocol parser. One state transition must preserve a counterintuitive wire-compatibility rule, and extracting it would split the state machine across files.
evals.expected_output: Readable structure with one narrow comment for the compatibility rule.
expectations: First uses names and structure to make the state machine readable
Adds only the narrow comment that explains what the code cannot
Adds no comments that narrate ordinary control flow

evals.prompt: Reformat this long expression where the result of one call is passed directly into another call.
evals.expected_output: A nested call on its own line or named, with the behaviour unchanged.
expectations: Places a nested call on its own line or gives its result a descriptive intermediate name
Preserves the original types, argument order, and behavior
Does not extract trivial methods merely to shorten the expression

evals.prompt: Clean up these declarations in a language without a dedicated write-code reference. The assignments and object keys have extra spaces so their separators line up vertically.
evals.expected_output: Single spacing with semantic blank lines kept.
expectations: Removes padding added only to align assignments or keys vertically
Preserves semantic blank lines between unrelated logical phases
Does not collapse distinct phases into one dense block

evals.prompt: Write a PHP method in a project with a configured formatter. Follow the PHP coding standard while writing, then format the completed code to match the project.
evals.expected_output: PHP written to the standard and finished with the project formatter.
expectations: Uses PER as the writing baseline for PHP
Runs the project's configured formatter after writing the implementation
Accepts formatter output for final mechanical layout

evals.prompt: Refactor this PHP method: a nested ternary supplies a default, and a long condition combines type assertions with several || checks.
evals.expected_output: Null coalescing, guards or match, and named checks.
expectations: Uses null coalescing, guard clauses, or match in place of the ternary
Names each check before the condition rather than leaving a wrapped || expression

evals.prompt: Clean up PHP that calls a method chain of two links on one line and passes a nested method call as one of several arguments.
evals.expected_output: Each link after the first on its own line and the nested call hoisted into a variable.
expectations: Keeps the receiver and first link on one line and starts each later link on its own line
Hoists the nested call into a named variable
Puts each argument of a multi-argument named call on its own line

evals.prompt: Check whether the string 'first' exists in a PHP array of elements, then find an invoice ID in an array of IDs.
evals.expected_output: Strict comparison on both lookups.
expectations: Passes true for the strict argument to in_array
Passes true for the strict argument to array_search
Does not rely on loose equality or implicit coercion

evals.prompt: Implement a PHP Action we own that accepts nested keyed invoice input and must return success or failure with optional invoice data.
evals.expected_output: An input DTO and an ActionResult.
expectations: Replaces the keyed input shape with a purpose-named DTO
Returns an ActionResult that represents success, failure, and optional returned data
Does not use a DTO merely because the Action returns data

evals.prompt: Translate a GatewayUnavailable exception into the domain's PaymentFailed exception in PHP.
evals.expected_output: A narrow catch and a domain exception carrying the cause.
expectations: Catches the narrow infrastructure exception rather than Throwable
Throws the purpose-named domain exception rather than a generic Exception
Passes the caught exception as previous when constructing the domain exception
Does not both log and rethrow the same failure at this boundary

evals.prompt: Collect the responses of each batch in a PHP foreach and return them as one flat array.
evals.expected_output: Pieces collected in the loop and merged once after it.
expectations: Collects each batch's responses in the loop
Merges once after the loop
Does not call array_merge on each iteration

evals.prompt: Clean up this method whose validation, transformation, and persistence statements currently run together without spacing.
evals.expected_output: Blank lines between phases and none between every statement.
expectations: Keeps statements serving the same step together
Separates distinct logical blocks with vertical whitespace
Puts a blank line before each if, loop, or match
Does not insert blank lines between every statement

evals.prompt: This method has five parameters and four returns, but each return is a short guard and the complete flow fits on one screen. Clean it up.
evals.expected_output: Limits treated as a prompt to look for a seam, not a reason to split mechanically.
expectations: Looks for a seam instead of treating the limits as automatic failures
Extracts a cohesive responsibility if one exists
Does not split by line count or replace a readable flow with trivial indirection

evals.prompt: Add a Laravel endpoint in a project whose documented naming conventions and linter differ from common Laravel defaults.
evals.expected_output: Project naming, with Laravel guidance applied to framework behaviour only.
expectations: Uses the naming conventions documented by the project
Satisfies the formatter, linter, and static analysis rules that govern naming
Does not rename existing or new symbols to match Laravel defaults

evals.prompt: Persist a new Laravel model from already validated request data.
evals.expected_output: Explicit attribute assignment.
expectations: Assigns each intended model attribute explicitly
Does not pass the validated array to create or fill

evals.prompt: Read a nested array value, fetch runtime configuration, and split a collection into accepted and rejected records in Laravel.
evals.expected_output: data_get, config(), and partition.
expectations: Uses data_get for the nested array access
Uses config for runtime configuration and never env outside a configuration file
Uses partition instead of duplicating filter and reject passes

evals.prompt: Issuing an invoice saves it and records its ledger entry. Both writes must succeed or fail together.
evals.expected_output: One transaction in the orchestrating layer.
expectations: Places one DB::transaction around the complete business operation
Keeps the transaction in the layer that orchestrates both writes

evals.prompt: Return a Laravel API resource whose customer relation is optional and whose reference field may be null.
evals.expected_output: A JsonResource using conditional field APIs.
expectations: Uses a JsonResource rather than returning a model or raw array from the controller
Uses whenLoaded for the optional customer relation
Uses whenNotNull for the nullable reference

evals.prompt: Handle a browser input event in TypeScript and save the target value. The event target is not statically known to be an input.
evals.expected_output: A narrowed target with no assertion.
expectations: Narrows event.target with instanceof HTMLInputElement
Does not assert event.target with as HTMLInputElement

evals.prompt: Map every member of a closed TypeScript invoice-status union to its handler.
evals.expected_output: An as-const map and an exhaustive Record.
expectations: Defines each variant literal once in an as-const value map
Derives the union from the value map
Uses Record keyed by the union so a missing handler is a type error

evals.prompt: In a Vue component, keep an invoice total updated from a reactive list of line items.
evals.expected_output: A computed total.
expectations: Uses computed for the invoice total
Does not use watch or watchEffect to update other reactive state

evals.prompt: In a Bash function, assign the output of git rev-parse to a local repository_root and stop if git fails.
evals.expected_output: A separate local declaration and assignment.
expectations: Declares repository_root separately from the command substitution
Handles or propagates the git failure
Does not mask failure with local, readonly, declare, or export

evals.prompt: Run a Bash function for every file below a directory, including names with spaces and newlines.
evals.expected_output: A NUL-delimited find loop with quoted expansions.
expectations: Uses find with -print0
Reads with IFS= read -r -d ''
Quotes the filename passed to the function
Does not parse ls

evals.prompt: Add a Bash function with a local output directory, an exported cache directory, and a force option flag.
evals.expected_output: CSE 374-style names without a boolean prefix on the option variable.
expectations: Uses snake_case for the function and local variable
Uses ALL_CAPS for the exported environment variable
Names the option-state variable force

evals.prompt: Format a Go function that loads a customer, checks that error, creates an invoice, checks that error, saves it, and returns it.
evals.expected_output: One blank line between each operation and its error guard.
expectations: Puts one blank line between each operation and the guard checking its error
Wraps each error with the failed operation in lower-case text without trailing punctuation
Does not insert blank lines between every statement

evals.prompt: A Go invoice package can consume either the production Postgres store or a runtime-selected in-memory store. Add the abstraction at their boundary.
evals.expected_output: A narrow interface in the consuming package.
expectations: Defines the interface in the consuming package
Keeps the implementation constructor's return type concrete

evals.prompt: Add context to a Go storage error. Callers may classify the underlying not-found error.
evals.expected_output: %w wrapping where callers classify, handled once.
expectations: Wraps with %w because callers use errors.Is or errors.As
Handles each error once rather than logging and returning it

evals.prompt: Start a long-running Go processor in the background and make shutdown reliable.
evals.expected_output: A caller-owned goroutine tied to context cancellation and awaited.
expectations: Gives the goroutine an owner that waits for it, such as errgroup
Propagates the caller's context into blocking work

evals.prompt: Implement a Go accessor for an invoice ID and a validity predicate.
evals.expected_output: InvoiceID and Valid.
expectations: Preserves ID as a Go initialism
Omits the Get prefix from the accessor
Names the predicate Valid rather than IsValid

evals.prompt: While adding a refund reason field, the checks run after the edit report a formatter failure and a static analysis error on the file just changed.
evals.expected_output: Failures fixed before the next edit.
expectations: Fixes the reported failures on that file before editing another file

evals.prompt: The export fix is done and the edit checks are clean. Hand it back.
evals.expected_output: Verification run via verify and an Evidence section.
expectations: Runs verify (including verify-changes.sh handoff and end-to-end checks) before reporting
Ends with an Evidence section listing each command and the output that shows its result

evals.prompt: Orders placed just before midnight are showing up on the wrong day in the daily sales report. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: A failing check first, then a loop to green.
expectations: Writes a check that reproduces the bug before changing production code
Runs the check and shows it failing for the reported reason before implementing
Reruns the check after each attempt and keeps fixing until it passes, without stopping to ask between attempts

evals.prompt: Bump the build so it targets the newer runtime version the deploy platform now requires.
evals.expected_output: A command and its expected output as the check.
expectations: States the end state as a command and the output that means it passed
Does not invent a unit test for a change no test can meaningfully cover
Loops on the command until it shows the expected result

evals.prompt: The test you wrote for the rounding fix still fails after three attempts. The assertion expects 10.05 and the code returns 10.04.
evals.expected_output: The check kept as strict as written while the code is fixed.
expectations: Leaves the check's expected result unchanged
Does not skip, delete, or loosen the test to make it pass
Keeps working on the code until the check passes
